idle.title: Press a scenario to send an alert into the process
idle.plain: Think of a hospital front desk. A patient walks in, a nurse checks them, a standard treatment is tried only if it is safe to undo, and a doctor steps in whenever the nurse is unsure. This page shows the same thing for a software incident.
idle.technical: Start publishes the message "Alert (monitoring/event system)" to Camunda 8. The message start event creates a process instance of Process_Incident. Everything you see is read live from the engine's REST API.

done.title: The incident is closed, and a record exists
done.plain: Every path ends the same way: a written record was made before the case closed. That is the rule the diagram enforces, not a habit.
done.technical: The instance reached an end event. Every path passes Task_Postmortem first, so workers/postmortems/<processInstanceKey>.md exists for each run.

A.label: 1. A fix that works
A.plain: A payment service is failing because a cache server is overloaded. The agent finds the standard fix, applies it and checks the result.
A.incident: Payment API is returning HTTP 500 for roughly 12% of checkout requests over the last 10 minutes, and the error rate is climbing. The Redis cache node backing the session store is pegged at 100% CPU. No other services are affected yet.
A.watch: Watch for: the agent acts alone, a second check agrees.

B.label: 2. Nothing matches
B.plain: Photo uploads are slow in one region and nothing is logged as an error. No standard fix fits, so a person must decide.
B.incident: Users in the EU region are reporting that photo uploads in the mobile app are slower than usual, sometimes taking a full minute. No errors are being logged, and the same feature works normally in other regions.
B.watch: Watch for: the agent does nothing, and says why.

C.label: 3. A fix that fails
C.plain: The same cache problem, but this time the standard fix does not work. The agent must notice, and hand over instead of trying again.
C.incident: Payment API is returning HTTP 500 for roughly 12% of checkout requests over the last 10 minutes, and the error rate is climbing. The Redis cache node backing the session store is pegged at 100% CPU. No other services are affected yet.
C.watch: Watch for: a fix that fails, and a hand-over instead of a retry.

Task_HumanTriage.ask: No standard fix matched, or it was not safe to undo. You are the on-call engineer. What did you find?
Task_HumanTriage.technical: User task. Completing it sets triageOutcome. The Tasklist at the engine's own address shows the same task.

defaults.B: Cold CDN edge cache in the EU region. Warmed the cache; no playbook needed.
defaults.default: Diagnosed by hand; resolved without a playbook.

Task_EscalateHuman.ask: The agent's fix did not clear the problem, so it stopped and handed over. You are the on-call engineer. What did you find?
Task_EscalateHuman.technical: User task. The independent verification said "not resolved" (verified = false), so the default flow of Gateway_Resolved routes here. Completing it sets triageOutcome.

defaults.default: The restart did not help. A runaway session-export job was holding the cache. Stopped the job.

Task_ConfirmRootCause.ask: The agent thinks this looks like a known, repeating problem. You decide whether it is worth fixing for good.
Task_ConfirmRootCause.technical: User task behind Gateway_CSISignal (clusterScore >= 0.6). Completing it sets rootCauseConfirmed and csiDecision. A human always prioritises; the agent never funds an improvement.

defaults.default: Undersized cache tier and no eviction policy. Fund a permanent fix: resize it and add an eviction policy.

StartEvent_Alert.title: An alert arrives
StartEvent_Alert.plain: A monitoring system raises its hand: something is wrong. It is like a patient walking in the front door.
StartEvent_Alert.technical: Message start event. The alert text arrives as the variable incidentDescription.

Task_Enrich.title: Gathering context
Task_Enrich.plain: A nurse takes a quick history before anyone decides anything. This step is plain code. No AI is involved, and none is pretended.
Task_Enrich.technical: Service task, job type enrich-event. Keyword tagging puts the incident into a service area. Deterministic.

Task_ClassifySeverity.title: How serious is it?
Task_ClassifySeverity.plain: The triage nurse picks one level: cosmetic, minor, major or critical. The AI is good at this kind of reading, and it also says how sure it is.
Task_ClassifySeverity.technical: Business rule task, job type typesafe-classify-severity. A TypeSafe Choice picks one of four severities. Confidence shows how concentrated the answer is. It is not permission to act.

Task_MatchPattern.title: Is there a standard fix for this?
Task_MatchPattern.plain: Code first picks the one standard treatment that looks closest. Then the AI answers a single yes-or-no question: does this case really match that treatment? Whether the fix can be undone comes from the playbook itself, never from the AI.
Task_MatchPattern.technical: Business rule task, job type typesafe-match-pattern. Code selects a candidate playbook (IDF-weighted word overlap over fixtures/playbooks.json). A TypeSafe Noul returns one probability that the incident matches it. reversible is read from the playbook.

Gateway_AutoCandidate.title: Gate 1: may the agent act alone?
Gateway_AutoCandidate.plain: Two things must both be true: the agent is very sure, and the fix can be undone. If either fails, a person takes over. A sure agent still may not do something that cannot be reversed.
Gateway_AutoCandidate.technical: Exclusive gateway. Condition: =matchConfidence >= 0.8 and reversible = true. The default flow goes to Task_HumanTriage. The gate is a visible condition in the diagram, not the model's output triggering the next step.

Task_AutoRemediate.title: Applying the standard fix
Task_AutoRemediate.plain: The agent carries out the playbook. In this lab the fix is simulated, because there is no real server to restart.
Task_AutoRemediate.technical: Service task, job type auto-remediate. Reads the matched playbook, "runs" it, and returns a synthetic post-action reading. Set fixOutcome to works or fails to pin the result; otherwise it works 80% of the time.

Task_VerifyFix.title: Did it work?
Task_VerifyFix.plain: A second, separate check looks at the numbers after the fix. The step that acted does not get to mark its own homework.
Task_VerifyFix.technical: Business rule task, job type typesafe-verify-fix. A second TypeSafe Noul, with the post-action reading as its input. Probability >= 0.7 becomes verified = true.

Gateway_Resolved.title: Gate 2: is it really fixed?
Gateway_Resolved.plain: Fixed, and the record continues. Not fixed, and a person is called with the full story. The agent never just tries again in silence.
Gateway_Resolved.technical: Exclusive gateway. Condition: =verified = true. The default flow escalates to Task_EscalateHuman.

Task_HumanTriage.title: A person takes over
Task_HumanTriage.plain: The case goes to the on-call engineer, who decides what to do. Nothing has been changed yet.
Task_HumanTriage.technical: User task in the Human lane. Sets triageOutcome.

Task_EscalateHuman.title: The fix failed, so a person takes over
Task_EscalateHuman.plain: The agent noticed its fix did not work and handed over with everything it knew.
Task_EscalateHuman.technical: User task in the Human lane. Reached through the default flow of Gateway_Resolved. Sets triageOutcome.

Gateway_Converge.title: All paths join here
Gateway_Converge.plain: Fixed by the agent, solved by a person, or handed over after a failed fix: every case now goes to the same next step.
Gateway_Converge.technical: Converging exclusive gateway. No condition on the inbound flows.

Task_Postmortem.title: Writing the record, always
Task_Postmortem.plain: Every case gets a written record, whatever happened. There is no route through the diagram that skips it.
Task_Postmortem.technical: Service task, job type generate-postmortem. Writes workers/postmortems/<processInstanceKey>.md from every variable so far. Deterministic.

Task_ClusterProblem.title: Have we seen this before?
Task_ClusterProblem.plain: The agent compares this case with known, repeating problems and scores how closely it matches each one. Like a ward checking whether this is the third case of the same infection.
Task_ClusterProblem.technical: Business rule task, job type typesafe-cluster-problem. One TypeSafe request carries one Score question per known cluster (ordered three-level scale). The best score is normalised to clusterScore. A cluster marked recurring: false forces it to 0.

Gateway_CSISignal.title: Gate 3: worth a person's attention?
Gateway_CSISignal.plain: A strong match goes to a person to decide whether to fix the root cause. A weak match is closed, but the record still says so.
Gateway_CSISignal.technical: Exclusive gateway. Condition: =clusterScore >= 0.6. The default flow closes with no CSI action.

Task_ConfirmRootCause.title: A person decides about a lasting fix
Task_ConfirmRootCause.plain: Only a person can decide whether a problem is worth fixing for good. The agent suggests; it never spends the money.
Task_ConfirmRootCause.technical: User task in the Human lane. Sets rootCauseConfirmed and csiDecision.

End_ClosedNoAction.title: Closed, no further action
End_ClosedNoAction.plain: The case is closed. It was not a repeating problem, and the record says so.
End_ClosedNoAction.technical: End event. Reached through the default flow of Gateway_CSISignal.

End_ClosedCSI.title: Closed, improvement proposed
End_ClosedCSI.plain: The case is closed, and a person has made a call about preventing it next time.
